title: Graph Neural Networks for Natural Language Processing: A Survey
venue: Foundations and Trends® in Machine Learning
method: Survey of GNNs for NLP
findings: Organises GNN-for-NLP work by graph construction, representation learning and encoder-decoder models (abstract not retrieved; title and venue only)

title: Large Language Models on Graphs: A Comprehensive Survey
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
method: Survey: LLMs on pure, text-attributed and text-paired graphs; LLM as predictor, encoder, aligner
datasets: Summarises open-source code and benchmark datasets
findings: States that whether LLM text reasoning generalises to graphs is underexplored (abstract)

title: Fake news detection: A survey of graph neural network methods
method: Survey of GNN methods for fake news detection
findings: Abstract not read; cited as evidence that the area is surveyed

title: Fake News Detection Through Graph-based Neural Networks: A Survey
method: Survey: knowledge-driven, propagation-based and heterogeneous social-context graph methods for fake news detection
findings: Discusses challenges and open problems of graph-based fake news detection (abstract)

title: Harnessing Explanations: LLM-to-LM Interpreter for Enhanced Text-Attributed Graph Representation Learning
method: TAPE: prompt an LLM (the repository distributes 'GPT responses'; exact model version not checked) for zero-shot predictions plus explanations; an LM interprets them into node features for a GNN
datasets: Cora, PubMed, ogbn-arxiv, tape-arxiv23 (repository calls it arxiv_2023)
findings: State-of-the-art on these TAG datasets and 2.88x faster training than the closest baseline on ogbn-arxiv (abstract)
limitations: Repository LM example uses 4 GPUs; environment pinned to PyTorch 1.12.1 / CUDA 11.3; precomputed GPT responses are provided for download (README, read 2026-10-17)

title: STAGE: Simplified Text-Attributed Graph Embeddings Using Pre-trained LLMs
venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models (KaLLM 2024)
method: STAGE: use pre-trained LLMs only as embedding generators for node text, then ensemble GNNs
datasets: Node classification benchmarks (not named in abstract)
findings: Competitive results with a simpler pipeline than multi-stage prompting methods (abstract)

title: Exploring the Potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) in Learning on Graphs
method: Systematic study of LLMs-as-Enhancers and LLMs-as-Predictors for node classification
datasets: Cora, PubMed, ogbn-arxiv, ogbn-products and others
findings: Section 7.1 Finding 3 (full text): a potential test data leakage problem on ogbn-arxiv; LLM-as-predictor evaluation used 200 sampled test nodes because of API cost
limitations: Section 7.2/7.3 (full text): querying LLM APIs at least N times for N nodes makes large graphs costly; test data may appear in LLM training corpora

title: Can LLMs Effectively Leverage Graph Structural Information through Prompts, and Why?
method: Curates a leakage-free dataset (arxiv-2023, test nodes are 2023 arXiv CS papers) and compares LLM prompting with and without structure
datasets: arxiv-2023 (33,868 nodes, 305,672 edges, per repository README), ogbn-arxiv, Cora, PubMed
findings: No substantial evidence that LLM performance is due to data leakage; LLMs read neighbourhood prompts as context paragraphs; label-relevant phrases help most (abstract)
limitations: Repository template targets ChatGPT through the OpenAI API only; no licence stated (README)

title: GLBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Graph with Large Language Models
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37
method: GLBench: benchmark of GraphLLM methods vs GNN baselines with consistent splits, supervised and zero-shot
findings: LLM-as-enhancer methods most robust; LLM-as-predictor less effective; no clear scaling law; a simple zero-shot baseline beats several tailored models (abstract)

title: When Do LLMs Help With Node Classification? A Comprehensive Analysis
method: LLMNodeBed: codebase and testbed, 8 LLM-based algorithms incl. TAPE, 8 classic baselines, 3 learning paradigms, >2,700 models
datasets: 10 homophilic + 4 heterophilic TAGs (Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, arXiv, WikiCS, Instagram, Reddit, Books, Photo, Computer, Cornell, Texas, Wisconsin, Washington)
findings: LLM methods help clearly in semi-supervised settings, marginally in supervised ones (abstract). Full text: TAPE uses Mistral-7B by default; replacing it with GPT-4o helps by up to 4% on Pubmed semi-supervised and the gap narrows with supervision; TAPE took 5.9 h on Pubmed on one H100-80G
limitations: Conclusion (full text): limited exploration of LLMs on heterophilic graphs and scarcity of text-rich heterophilic datasets. No discussion of training-data leakage found in the full text

title: Classic GNNs are Strong Baselines: Reassessing GNNs for Node Classification
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37
method: Re-tunes GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE against graph transformers on 18 datasets
findings: Classic GNNs with light tuning match or beat graph transformers on 17 of 18 datasets (abstract)

title: Does syntax matter? A strong baseline for Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis with RoBERTa
venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies
method: Compares parser trees with trees induced from fine-tuned RoBERTa inside ABSA graph models (ASGCN, PWCN, RGAT); plain RoBERTa baseline
datasets: Six ABSA datasets in four languages
findings: FT-RoBERTa induced trees beat parser trees; a pure RoBERTa model outperforms or approximates previous SOTA (abstract)
limitations: Official repository has no licence and no seed control was found by the automated check; last push 2023-03-08

title: Syntax-Enhanced Pretrained Language Models for Aspect-Level Sentiment Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
method: SE-BERT: syntax-enhanced transformer layers replacing BERT's final layers
findings: Abstract states that existing methods improve aspect-level sentiment classification by adding syntactic GCN layers on BERT

title: On the Robustness of Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis: Rethinking Model, Data, and Training
method: Universal-syntax GCN plus synthetic data and adversarial/contrastive training for ABSA robustness
findings: Strong in-house ABSA models generalise poorly to challenging contexts (abstract)

title: User Preference-aware Fake News Detection
venue: Proceedings of the 44th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
method: UPFD: joint news content and user-engagement graph modelling with GNNs
datasets: UPFD PolitiFact (314 graphs, 157 fake) and GossipCop (5,464 graphs, 2,732 fake), per repository README
findings: Releases code and data as a benchmark for GNN-based fake news detection (abstract)
limitations: README states no run count, split or seed; repository licence Apache-2.0

title: Revisiting Fake News Detection: Towards Temporality-aware Evaluation by Leveraging Engagement Earliness
venue: Proceedings of the Eighteenth ACM International Conference on Web Search and Data Mining
method: Temporality-aware evaluation of social-graph fake news detection; DAWN edge reweighting by engagement earliness
findings: Conventional methods lose discriminative power sharply when trained only on data available up to a point in time (abstract)

title: Less is More: Unseen Domain Fake News Detection via Causal Propagation Substructures
method: CSDA: causal propagation substructures for out-of-domain fake news detection
findings: 7-16% accuracy improvement on OOD fake news (abstract)

title: GNN-RAG: Graph Neural Retrieval for Large Language Model Reasoning
method: GNN-RAG: a GNN (ReaRev) retrieves answer candidates from a KG subgraph; shortest paths are verbalised for an LLM reader
findings: Full text: tuned LLaMA2-Chat-7B reader reaches WebQSP Hit 85.7 / F1 71.3; Table 5 shows retrieval also lifts Flan-T5-xl (WebQSP Hit 31.0 to 74.5)
limitations: Full text: assumes the KG subgraph contains the answer nodes; entity-linking errors and disconnected KG parts give empty paths. GNN runs used an RTX-3090 with 128 GB RAM; LLM runs used 4 A100 GPUs

title: RPO-RAG: Aligning Small LLMs with Relation-aware Preference Optimization for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
method: RPO-RAG: relation-aware preference optimisation and answer-centred prompts for small-LLM KG RAG
findings: States prior KG-RAG work relies on large LLMs or backbones above 7B, leaving sub-7B models underexplored (abstract)

title: HeTGB: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Heterophilic Text-Attributed Graphs
method: HeTGB: benchmark of five heterophilic text-attributed graphs evaluating GNNs, PLMs and co-training
findings: Shows utility of text in heterophilic graphs and limits of existing models (abstract)

title: Exploring the Potential of Large Language Models for Heterophilic Graphs
method: LLM-enhanced edge discriminator and edge reweighting for heterophilic graphs, with distillation to smaller models
findings: LLMs can improve node classification on heterophilic graphs (abstract)

title: A critical look at the evaluation of GNNs under heterophily: Are we really making progress?
method: Critique of heterophily benchmarks; new heterophilous datasets
findings: Duplicate nodes cause train-test leakage; standard GNNs usually beat specialised models on the new datasets (abstract)

title: Intruding with Words: Towards Understanding Graph Injection Attacks at the Text Level
method: Text-level graph injection attacks
findings: Title and abstract record retrieved; studied as closest work for the robustness candidate

title: Are LLM-Enhanced Graph Neural Networks Robust Against Poisoning Attacks?
venue: 2026 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
method: Poisoning attacks on LLM-enhanced GNNs (IEEE S&P 2026)
findings: Title-level match for the robustness candidate

title: Unveiling the Vulnerability of Graph-LLMs: An Interpretable Multi-Dimensional Adversarial Attack on TAGs
venue: Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026
method: Interpretable multi-dimensional adversarial attack on TAGs (WWW 2026)
findings: Title-level match for the robustness candidate

title: Robustness in Text-Attributed Graph Learning: Insights, Trade-offs, and New Defenses
method: Unified robustness evaluation of GNNs, robust GNNs and GraphLLMs under text, structure and hybrid perturbations; SFT-auto defence
findings: Text-structure robustness trade-offs; GNN robustness depends on the text encoder; GraphLLMs vulnerable to training-data corruption (abstract)

title: RDGCN: Reinforced Dependency Graph Convolutional Network for Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis
method: RDGCN: reinforced dependency GCN for ABSA
findings: Example of continued dependency-GCN ABSA work after 2021

title: Multi-View Attention Syntactic Enhanced Graph Convolutional Network for Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis
method: Multi-view attention syntactic enhanced GCN for ABSA
findings: Example of continued dependency-GCN ABSA work after 2021
